output.summary: Sub-field checkpoint selectors (`.change`, `.tree`) render {commit, base, change, diff} (tree only when selected) through the same source resolve used, with an equality guard and bare-value fallback; approve items gain commit and base; fingerprints are untouched. shrink never blobs a checkpoint view, never grows a card, and first recovers truly redundant bytes (argv duplicates, duplicated commands list, 120-char blob previews, correction full.summary), with a key summary instead of `{` for blobbed dicts. Card inputs selected by a checkpoint's .change or .tree now show the producer's {commit, base, change, diff} (tree only for .tree). The checkpoint comes from the same source resolve used and is shown only when it matches the selected value; otherwise the card falls back to the bare value. Fingerprints are unchanged, and approve items gain commit and base. shrink never blobs a checkpoint view and never makes a card larger. It applies steps in order (drop argv, point context.commands at commands_to_run, clip blob summaries to 120 characters, blob the largest inline text) and keeps only steps that reduce size. findings.text: F1 Card size budget does not hold. At 54d7e83 the real implement card (card-1014-implement) is 4,621 canonical bytes after shrink has already blobbed the prompt and all instructions. shrink stops and returns an oversized card (test_card_shape_and_size already allows 4096+2000). A sub-field checkpoint view adds about 303 bytes, so shrink immediately blobs it into {summary:'{', blob, read}, which shows less than today's bare id. review_impl (3 instruction blobs, doc, checks, two views) works out to about 4.7 KB, so both views get blobbed. Consequence: the spec acceptance (review_impl carries commit/base/diff) fails on real cards, and the design's journey test either fails or passes only on fixture-sized cards. Fix: exempt checkpoint views from shrink (or blob them last) and recover space elsewhere (truncate artifact summaries, which shrink never touches today; drop duplicate argv/command forms), optionally drop tree when tree is not the selected sub-field, give blob_view a useful summary, and state the budget with measured real-size implement/review_impl cards, or record an explicit limit decision and test the actual bound.

spec:
Bug found while dogfooding Release 1. The default graph binds code inputs by sub-field so that fingerprints follow the right identity: review_tests, implement and review_impl take `test_design.tests.change`; review_impl and approve_merge take `implement.code.change`; run_tests and integrate take `implement.code.tree`. But card.value_of renders `checkpoint_view` (commit, base, tree, change, diff command) only when the selector has no path. These cards therefore show a bare patch id or tree id, which is not a commit and cannot be diffed. The G1014 review_tests reviewer could not locate the tests and had to dig the commit out of goal.json. Every code review and the merge approval would be equally blind. Approve items (render.py) may have the same gap: check.

Outcome:
- A card input whose selector names a checkpoint output plus a sub-field (`change` or `tree`) renders the full checkpoint view of that output, so the reviewer gets the commit and the diff command. The fingerprint still uses only the selected sub-field. Rendering must not change any input fingerprint.
- Human approve items show the same commit and diff.
- The card size budget (4 KB) still holds.

Acceptance:
- Engine tests: a review_tests card and a review_impl card each carry commit, base and diff for their tests and code inputs, and the diff command runs and shows the goal's own changes.
- The approve_merge item shows the code commit.
- Fingerprints of the affected nodes are unchanged before and after the fix, so no in-flight goal goes stale.
- The renamed-graph variant passes.
- A regression test reads each agent card of a full journey and checks that every checkpoint-typed input carries a commit that `git cat-file -t` resolves to a commit.
title: Show the full checkpoint on cards for inputs selected by change or tree
